classification.difficultyReason: Follow the scaffolded parts to interpret the limit, verify the supplied model, establish the given parameter and solve a threshold equation with a whole-year interpretation.

content.prompt: The population $P$ of a bird species is modelled by the differential equation $\dfrac{dP}{dt}=-k(P-Q)$, where $t$ is time in years and $k>0$ and $Q$ are fixed constants.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the significance of the value of $Q$ with respect to the population of an animal species in this model?

answer.short: $Q$ is the limiting population of the species.
answer.worked: Since $k>0$, $e^{-kt}\to0$ as $t\to\infty$. Hence $P\to Q$, so $Q$ is the limiting population of the species.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the equation $P=Q+Ae^{-kt}$ satisfies the differential equation.

answer.worked:
Differentiating $P=Q+Ae^{-kt}$ gives
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dP}{dt}&=-Ake^{-kt}.\end{align*}$$
Separately,
$$\begin{align*}-k(P-Q)&=-k(Q+Ae^{-kt}-Q)\\&=-k(Ae^{-kt})\\&=-Ake^{-kt}.\end{align*}$$
Both sides are equal, so the equation satisfies the differential equation.

children.label: c
children.prompt:
Initially, there are 1000 birds. After ten years the population has doubled. After an extended period of time, the population of the bird species plateaus at 8000.

Show that $k=\dfrac{1}{10}\ln\left(\dfrac{7}{6}\right)$.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Hence, find the first whole number of years after which the population exceeds half of its limiting population.

answer.worked:
Half the limiting population is $4000$ birds. First find when the population reaches this value:
$$\begin{align*}4000&=8000-7000e^{-kt}\\-4000&=-7000e^{-kt}\\e^{-kt}&=\frac47\\-kt&=\ln\left(\frac47\right)\\t&=\frac{\ln(4/7)}{-k}\\&=\frac{10\ln(7/4)}{\ln(7/6)}\\&\approx36.30\text{ years}.\end{align*}$$
The population is increasing, so it exceeds $4000$ for $t>\dfrac{10\ln(\frac{7}{4})}{\ln(\frac{7}{6})}$. The first whole number of years is therefore $37$.
